title: Finite-family coefficient bad set
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$. For $S\in\mathcal F$, the bad set consists of arrays assigning to each member of $\mathcal F$ a batch of $m$ cube inputs, where $m$ is the sample count obtained using accuracy $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal F|)$ and confidence $1/(10|\mathcal F|)$, for which the empirical Fourier coefficient on $S$ differs from its true coefficient by at least $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal F|)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a finite nonempty family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
